title: Where the Weight Presses: The Centre of Pressure, the Zero Moment Point of an Accelerating Body, and the Acceleration the Feet Can Allow

questions.question: Where does a body that accelerates forward press on the ground?
options: Ahead of its centre of mass, by h over g times the acceleration
Directly under its centre of mass, whatever the acceleration
Behind its centre of mass, by h over g times the acceleration
Behind its centre of mass, by the acceleration times the time step
questions.explanation: To accelerate forward the ground has to push from behind. On a body 0.27 m high, 3 m/s2 moved the point 83 mm back.

questions.question: The centre of pressure must be:
options: Under the centre of mass
Under the foot carrying the most
At the centre of the feet
Inside the polygon of the feet on the ground
questions.explanation: It is an average of the feet's places weighted by pushes that are all zero or more, and such an average cannot lie outside them.

questions.question: With four feet the acceleration allowed sideways was:
questions.explanation: g times the distance to the edge over the height. The feet are closer together side to side than fore and aft, so sideways gives less: 5.45 against 6.90.

questions.question: With two diagonal feet down:
options: 5.45 m/s2 is still allowed, across the line
Half the four footed figure is allowed
No acceleration is safe: the support is a line
Any acceleration along the line is allowed
questions.explanation: A line has no inside, so the margin is zero at best. A trot is not balanced in this sense; it is caught by the next pair of feet.

questions.question: What does a taller body do to the greatest acceleration?
options: Lowers it, since it goes as 1 over h
Raises it, since the feet have more leverage
Leaves it the same: only the feet's spread matters
Lowers it, in proportion to the square of the height
questions.explanation: The shift of the point is h over g times the acceleration, so for the same feet a body twice as high may accelerate half as hard.

questions.question: What does the body not do in this model?
options: Accelerate sideways
Turn, and change height
Stand on three feet
Press unevenly on its feet
questions.explanation: The formula assumes the body keeps its height and does not rotate. A body that turns has angular momentum that adds a term.
